subject: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-ops@example.com
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan

Team —

As we lock the Q4 launch window, I want a concise snapshot of where engineering and product land on the three launch pillars: runtime stability, model onboarding cadence, and partnership integrations (Orbit Cloud). Specifically I need:

- Sprint velocity (last 3 sprints) vs. forecast for remaining milestones
- Any open blockers that would push the end-to-end launch past 2026-11-18
- Mitigation options by impact/cost (canary window, feature gating, expanded partner assisted QA)

Attached is the template for the release matrix and a quick velocity export — please populate and reply with updates by EOD tomorrow so I can fold into the QBR pack.

Action: everyone on cc (internal) — add one line per risk and an ETA to resolve.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sprint-velocity-202610.pdf (report stub), release-matrix-Q4-2026.xlsx (matrix template)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan

David —

Quick summary from Product:
- Shipping scope trimmed to MLP (minimal launch product) to protect user flows for core customers (Acme + 2 pilot accounts).
- Feature-level de-scopes are marked in the attached release matrix under column "Must Ship" vs "Deferred".
- Risk: two outstanding UX reviews that may introduce rework (~3 dev days each) if feedback requires design changes.

I updated the release matrix with product-level priority and estimated impact. See Drive link.

Next steps: If eng needs a contingency for release day, propose we enable feature gates for non-core features and run a controlled canary with Acme for 72 hours post-launch.

Laura
Director, Product Management

To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@orbitcloud.io
Date: 2026-10-21T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan

Folks —

Engineering update (short):
- Velocity: sprints 11/12/13 completed story points = 82 / 88 / 79. Forecast for 2 remaining sprints before code-freeze is ~170 story points (conservative).
- Known blockers:
  1) Runtime stability regression in multi-tenant KV cache when sequence length > 2048 (root cause: cache eviction race). Investigating, rough ETA 6-8 business days for full fix; potential short-term mitigation: reduce prefetch window and add tighter evictions (config flag).
  2) Partner integration tests failing on Orbit Cloud auth handshake — dependency on their SDK 1.4.2; workaround available (manual token refresh) but requires QA cycles.
- Contingency: If the cache fix slips, we can ship with a guarded config that limits long sequences to dedicated instances and route high-latency customers to fallback models for 48–72 hrs.

Attached a short velocity export (sprint-velocity-202610.pdf) and filled the release matrix with technical notes.

Marcus
Engineering Director, Serving Runtime

Attachments: sprint-velocity-202610.pdf (velocity export)

> On 2026-10-21 11:03, Laura Bennett wrote:
> > David —
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan

Adding QA perspective —

- Orbit Cloud integration failures are reproducible in our staging harness; main failure mode is token refresh race under load. We've validated the manual token refresh workaround from Marcus; implementing it increases test coverage time by ~2 days.
- Coverage gaps: no automated smoke for KV eviction scenarios with sequence > 2k — manual tests show intermittent data corruption (low frequency but high impact).
- Recommendation: Prioritize automated smoke for sequence-length cache behavior (2 days), and schedule a focused 48-hr soak on a dedicated instance before canary.

I'll update the release matrix with QA risk scores. If leadership wants to err on caution, we should shift the public launch back 1 week to complete the soak.

Soojin
Sr. QA Manager

> On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 2:22 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan

Acknowledged. Quick notes from Program Management:
- I've consolidated the open risks into the release matrix and added an "impact / probability" column. Current forecast still shows launch target 2026-11-18 but with a 20% schedule risk if KV fix slips and Orbit SDK isn't updated.
- Proposed immediate: (1) we enable the guarded config flag and notify Acme about a short feature gate; (2) schedule a partner-run QA pass with Orbit Cloud next Tue; (3) set up a 1-hr leadership sync Friday to decide go/no-go after the soak results.

I'll book the Friday sync (15:00 PT) and share an updated one-pager for the QBR pack.

Mina
Sr. Program Manager

Date: 2026-10-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: sprint velocity snapshot & mitigation plan

Thanks all — good level of detail. Quick decisions for the QBR narrative and lock plan:

1) Do the guarded config and run the 48-hr dedicated soak. Mina, confirm when the instance will be available for soak and include the cost delta in the one-pager.
2) Marcus/QA: prioritize the automated smoke for KV edge-case (2 days) and run partner QA next Tue with Orbit; call out the mitigation steps (fallback routing + feature gate).
3) Laura: prepare a short customer-facing note for Acme explaining a limited feature gate and the timeline (to reassure them on availability).
4) Friday 15:00 PT leadership sync — I expect a go/no-go decision based on soak results.

I'll consolidate these into the QBR appendix and mark the schedule risk as "watch" with the contingency plan described. Good work — keep updates short and concrete so I can paste into the exec deck.

-David
David Kim
VP, Product Operations
